topic: Introduction to Topology: The Geometry of Rubber Sheets

sections.title: Prerequisites: Rigidity vs. Flexibility
lecture_lines: Geometry focuses on size, angles, and distances.
Topology ignores these, focusing on continuous deformation.
We never tear or glue objects.
animations: Display two rigid objects (cube and sphere) in #FFFFFF.
Highlight rigid boundary of cube and sphere with #FF5733.
Show continuous transformation of sphere into a flexible blob.

sections.title: The Core Concept: Homeomorphism
lecture_lines: Two shapes are topologically equivalent if deformed smoothly.
We call this transformation a homeomorphism.
A coffee mug can become a donut.
animations: Display a circle and a square side-by-side in #FFFFFF.
Animate the square morphing smoothly into a circle.

sections.title: The Topological Invariant: Holes
lecture_lines: Genus counts the number of holes.
Holes are preserved under continuous deformation.
Tearing or sealing changes the genus.
animations: Display a solid disk and a circle in #FFFFFF.
Highlight the 'hole' in the circle with #FFFF00.
Label the number of holes (0 vs 1).

sections.title: Real-World Application: The Hair Ball Theorem
lecture_lines: The Hairy Ball Theorem explains global properties.
You cannot comb a sphere's fur flat.
At least one cowlick must exist.
animations: Display a vector field covering a sphere surface in #FFFFFF.
Demonstrate impossibility of combing hair without singularities.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
lecture_lines: If you don't tear, holes define objects.
Equivalent shapes are fundamentally the same.
animations: Recap: Deformation, Homeomorphism, and Topological Invariants.
